scope: Primary-source factual context for frozen case; no probability, selection, or ranking.

case.question: Will Bernie Sanders be TIME Person of the Year 2026?

rule.source: frozen market criteria, exact identity above
rule.yes: Sanders explicitly named POY, OR if announced POY is concept/group/entity/thing, Sanders is directly associated and pictured on any official TIME cover announcing it. Multiple named people qualify.
rule.group_semantics: For a vague collective label, TIME feature article defines meaning; listed concepts/groups qualify only if equivalent. A listed concept/entity qualifies only if synonymous with announced POY.
rule.resolution: TIME announcing cover(s) primary; feature article may also be used. If no announcement by 2027-06-30 23:59 ET (EDT), No. Market metadata endDate 2027-01-01T04:59:00Z differs from fallback.

time_editorial.method: TIME says editors choose person/people with greatest influence during prior 12 months; editorial discretion. Official explainer updated 2025-12-11.
time_editorial.2026_calendar: TIME media kit observed 2026-10-20 lists digital category launches Dec 7-9 and POY digital release Dec 10, 2026; dates directional, subject to change/editorial discretion; not a shortlist date.
time_editorial.prior_group: TIME 2025 feature names “The Architects of AI” as POY, a prior group/concept selection. This establishes precedent only, not 2026 outcome.
time_editorial.current_2026_announcement: No 2026 POY announcement or shortlist is evidenced in captured sources as of observation; this is a bounded research result, not proof none exists.

sanders_2026.fact: TIME report on nationwide No Kings protests says St. Paul flagship rally had at least 50,000 attendees by midday and Sanders was among speakers; article describes his warning about authoritarianism/oligarchy. This is direct 2026 TIME coverage associating Sanders with a large protest movement; no POY implication.

Official bill text: Sanders introduced S.5493, Ban Artificial Superintelligence Act of 2026; read twice and referred to Senate Commerce, Science, and Transportation. Proposed act includes international agreements and allied coordination to prevent ASI, and global prevention policy; proposal, not enacted law.
Official bill text: Sanders introduced S.5384, Thirty-Two Hour Workweek Act; read twice and referred to HELP committee; proposal would amend FLSA standard workweek 40 to 32 hours.
